source: 外研社(新标准)选择性必修第一册 Unit 2 同主题完形(年轻作家的第一封拒稿信/永不放弃的长跑者/夏令营的吉米/黑暗中用餐/翻开新的一页/比赛失利后依然乐观)。用词限本单元/初中/常见词,答案唯一,选项同词性,与阅读/听力关不撞。答案位由 _balance 打散。

passages.title: Anna's First Rejection
passages.text: When Anna finished her first short story, she proudly sent it to a magazine. A week later, a letter arrived that began, "We regret to (1)____ you..." Like every young writer, she had (2)____ those very words. For a moment she felt like (3)____ up writing altogether. But then she remembered that many famous authors had (4)____ the same kind of rejection before they became successful. So, instead of throwing the letter away, she decided to (5)____ it on her wall as a reminder. Success, she told herself, (6)____ happens overnight. She kept (7)____ a little every day, and slowly her stories grew better. Two years later, a (8)____ finally agreed to print one of them. Anna learned that one letter could not decide her future, and that (9)____ is the real key to success. Today she still (10)____ writing stories for young readers.

questions.explanation: regret to inform 遗憾地通知。
dread 畏惧;她早就害怕这些字眼。
feel like giving up 想放弃;feel like 后接动名词。
face rejection 面对拒绝。
stick it on her wall 把它贴在墙上。
success rarely happens overnight 成功很少一蹴而就。
keep writing 坚持写;keep 后接动名词。
a publisher agreed to print 出版商同意付印。
perseverance is the key 坚持是关键。
enjoys writing 喜欢写;enjoy 后接动名词。

passages.title: The Runner Who Wouldn't Stop
passages.text: On the morning of the race, Daniel felt both nervous and (1)____. He had trained hard for months and did not want to give (2)____ now. The route was long, and after the first few kilometres his legs began to (3)____. Many runners around him slowed down, but Daniel kept (4)____ at a steady pace. Halfway through, he wanted to stop and (5)____, yet he reminded himself why he had started. "A medal is never (6)____ overnight," he thought. As the finish line came into (7)____, his heart filled with hope. He did not win first place, but he managed (8)____ the whole race, and that was a real success for him. His friends were (9)____ to inform him that he had beaten his own record. Daniel realised that the true (10)____ of the day was not a prize, but the courage never to give in.

questions.explanation: nervous and excited 紧张又兴奋。
give up 放弃。
his legs began to hurt 双腿开始疼。
kept running 一直跑;keep 后接动名词。
stop and rest 停下来休息。
a medal is never won overnight 奖牌绝非一夜得来。
come into view 进入视野。
manage to finish 设法跑完;manage 后接不定式。
delighted to inform 高兴地告知。
the true outcome 真正的收获/结果。

passages.title: Jamie at the Sports Camp
passages.text: Last summer, Jamie joined a sports camp, hoping (1)____ his character and make new friends. The camp was fun, but it was not (2)____ its challenges. Each day began with a five-kilometre run at six in the morning. At first Jamie could not (3)____ the whole route, and on the fourth day he was so tired that he did not even want (4)____ out of bed. He felt homesick and almost (5)____ his dad to take him home. But he did not give (6)____. Slowly, things got better. He learned to (7)____ each early morning instead of dreading it. By the end of the camp, Jamie felt much (8)____ and more confident than before. He had also made several good friends. Even though being a camper had its (9)____, Jamie felt the whole experience was truly (10)____. He came home tired but proud of what he had done.

questions.explanation: hope to build 希望塑造;hope 后接不定式。
not without its challenges 不无挑战。
could not finish the route 跑不完全程。
want to get out of bed 想起床;want 后接不定式。
almost phoned his dad 差点打电话给爸爸。
give up 放弃。
learned to enjoy each morning 学会享受每个清晨。
felt much stronger 觉得强壮多了。
had its challenges 有它的挑战。
truly worthwhile 真正值得。

passages.title: Dinner in the Dark
passages.text: Last week I went to a "dark restaurant", where guests eat in complete darkness and are (1)____ by blind waiters. My friend and I wanted to understand what it is like (2)____ blind, and we thought eating would be the hardest part. It was a difficult (3)____. Because we could not see anything, we kept (4)____ over our glasses and dropping our food. My sense of smell suddenly became more (5)____, and I ate much more slowly, trying to (6)____ what was on my plate. After failing (7)____ up any food with a fork, I decided to use my hands instead. Even then, I (8)____ most of the soup on my shirt. I felt rather (9)____, although of course no one could see me. When I finally left, I was still hungry, but I was much more (10)____ of the daily challenges that blind people bravely face.

questions.explanation: served by blind waiters 由盲人服务员招待。
what it is like to be blind 失明是什么感觉;固定句式用不定式。
a difficult meal 一顿艰难的饭。
kept knocking over our glasses 不断碰倒杯子;keep 后接动名词。
became more sensitive 变得更灵敏。
trying to guess 试着猜。
fail to pick up 没能夹起;fail 后接不定式。
spilled most of the soup 把汤洒了大半。
felt rather embarrassed 感到相当尴尬。
more aware of the challenges 更了解那些挑战。

passages.title: Turning Over a New Leaf
passages.text: At the start of the new term, Sam decided to turn over a new (1)____ and become a better student. In the past, he had often (2)____ his feet and put off doing his homework until the last minute. He also used to be a wet (3)____, spoiling the fun whenever his friends were excited about a project. This year, he promised (4)____ harder and to support the people around him. He started (5)____ a short plan every evening, so that he would no longer fall behind. Soon his classmates noticed the change and called him an eager (6)____, because he was always ready to help. Of course, change is never (7)____; there were days when Sam felt like giving (8)____. But he reminded himself that real success (9)____ trying again after each failure. Step by step, he became more (10)____ and confident, and his whole class felt happier for it.

questions.explanation: turn over a new leaf 翻开新的一页(改过自新)。
drag one's feet 拖拖拉拉。
a wet blanket 扫兴的人。
promise to work 答应努力;promise 后接不定式。
start making a plan 开始制定计划;此处用动名词亦可,语境为养成习惯。

give up 放弃。

passages.title: After the Contest
passages.text: When Dawei came out of the speech (1)____, his face looked sad and (2)____. He had hoped (3)____ first place, but the judges had chosen someone else. His friend Jack noticed at once that something was (4)____, so he asked Dawei what had happened. "I did my best, but I still didn't (5)____," Dawei said quietly. Jack reminded him that one result could not (6)____ his whole future. "Try (7)____ on the bright side," Jack said gently. "You spoke far better than last year." Slowly, Dawei began to (8)____ that he had actually enjoyed the experience and learned a lot. He had met new friends and felt more (9)____ on stage than ever before. By the time they walked home, Dawei was smiling again. He had learned that failure is only painful if you stop (10)____ in yourself.

questions.explanation: the speech contest 演讲比赛。

hope to win 希望获胜;hope 后接不定式。
